payload.text: Off-suit trump-rank cards rank equal to each other (DR-007 details).
payload.reason: Brief lists them at tier 4 without sub-ordering.

payload.text: When a follower has no cards in the led effective suit, they may play any cards to make up the count — no "must trump" rule.
payload.reason: Standard simplest variant; brief excludes throws and doesn't mandate over-trumping.

payload.text: "Final trick" of a round = whichever trick empties all four hands.
payload.reason: Brief's "If defenders win the final trick" wording.

payload.text: Six-character alphanumeric room codes are sufficient; collisions auto-retry.

payload.reason: README documents how to swap the LAN IP.

payload.text: Player ID is stable for the room's life; session ID rotates on `resumeSession`.
payload.reason: Cleaner separation; the brief implies both.

payload.text: No host-successor logic; if host disconnects the room idles until host returns or someone manually leaves.
payload.reason: Brief lists "remove disconnected unready players" as a *host* control; no symmetric "promote a new host" affordance.

payload.text: One in-flight intent per player; mutations per room are serialized.
Spectators / new joins after lobby phase are rejected.
payload.reason: Brief's join workflow requires lobby phase.

payload.text: Dealer must choose one of the four suits when all four pass; "no trump" is not allowed.
Kitty 2x bonus only on defenders winning the *final* trick (not other point-bearing tricks).
Round 1 dealer team is Team A (seats 0+2), starting at level 2.
payload.reason: Brief's "First round dealer is seat 0" + "both teams start at rank 2".

payload.text: Tractor adjacency uses the rule in DR-008.
payload.reason: The brief leaves trump tractor adjacency partly under-defined.

payload.decision: Delete the workbench's default `backend/`, `frontend/`, `docs/` placeholder directories and replace with the brief-specified pnpm monorepo layout (`packages/{client,server,shared}` + `tests/e2e`).
payload.rationale: The brief's directory shape is part of the acceptance criteria; the placeholders are scaffolding artifacts not requirements.
payload.alternatives_considered: keep `backend/` for the server and `frontend/` for the client and avoid `packages/`.
payload.why_not_alternatives: the brief specifies `/packages/` explicitly; honoring the brief beats accommodating scaffolding defaults.

payload.decision: Public room code is 6-character uppercase alphanumeric using the alphabet `[A-Z0-9]` minus visually-confusable characters (`0/O`, `1/I/L`). Effective alphabet of 32 → ≈1.07B codes.
payload.rationale: Short enough to read aloud; ambiguity-free for typing; collision-resistant for any plausible local-host count.
payload.why_not_alternatives: UUIDs are too long for verbal sharing; 4 chars collides too easily; word pairs add dependency on a wordlist and don't materially help here.

payload.decision: Reconnect token is `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString("base64url")` (43 chars). Stored only in SQLite + browser localStorage. Never broadcast.
payload.rationale: Cryptographically random; URL-safe; easy to compare server-side; aligned with the brief's "do not broadcast" rule.
payload.alternatives_considered: JWT with short TTL; shorter 16-byte token.
payload.why_not_alternatives: JWT adds signing-key management and clock skew; 16 bytes is enough but 32 costs nothing and matches common conventions.

payload.rationale: Simpler than `sqlite3` (callback-based) or `node:sqlite` (experimental in some LTS versions); fits a single-process Node server.
payload.why_not_alternatives: ORMs add overhead with no payoff at this scale; `sqlite3` async adds promise plumbing for no benefit; `node:sqlite` stability is Node-version-dependent.

payload.decision: Use React Router v6 for client routing.
payload.rationale: Two routes (`/` and `/room/:publicCode`); React Router is the standard.
payload.why_not_alternatives: TanStack adds type-routing we don't need; Wouter is fine but less familiar; no router would require manual history management for the join-by-link case.

payload.decision: Joker pairs are allowed only when both jokers are the same kind: two small jokers form a "small-joker pair"; two big jokers form a "big-joker pair". A small + a big do NOT form a pair.
payload.rationale: Matches standard Sheng Ji rules; matches the brief's "two cards with the same effective rank and same effective suit" definition (jokers have distinct effective rank via the `joker` discriminator).
payload.alternatives_considered: treat all jokers as one rank so any two jokers pair.
payload.why_not_alternatives: would let a small+big "pair" beat the big-joker pair, breaking the trump ordering.

payload.decision: Off-suit trump-rank cards (e.g. `2♠`, `2♦`, `2♣` when trump suit is hearts and trump rank is 2) are equal-ranked among each other. When two are played sequentially in a trick, first-played wins ties.
payload.rationale: Standard Sheng Ji; the brief lists them all at "tier 4" of the ordering without distinguishing.
payload.alternatives_considered: rank by suit (e.g. fixed C<D<H<S order); rank by player position.

payload.decision: For tractor adjacency, two pairs are "consecutive" if their effective ranks are adjacent in the trump-aware order *within the same effective suit*. Among non-trump suits, "adjacent" means adjacent in `RANKS` skipping the trump rank (since trump-rank cards in non-trump suits are trump, not in that non-trump suit). Among trump, "adjacent" means adjacent in the trump ordering, with off-suit trump-rank pairs treated as a single rank tier (so `2♣2♣ + 2♦2♦` cannot tractor; both are at the same tier). Jokers cannot extend a trump tractor (small-joker pair and big-joker pair are at distinct singleton tiers and are not "adjacent" to anything).
payload.rationale: Matches the brief's "consecutive pairs in the same effective suit" + "jokers do not form normal suit tractors" + the spirit of tractor play in the standard rules.
payload.alternatives_considered: allow joker-pair + trump-suit-trump-rank-pair to tractor; allow cross-suit off-suit trump-rank tractors.
payload.why_not_alternatives: opens the door to ill-defined orderings that fight the brief's explicit list.

payload.decision: New dealer after a round = the next player counter-clockwise from the current dealer if the dealer team retains, or the player on the defender team who is "to the right" of the previous dealer if the defender team takes over. Concretely: dealer-retention → dealer seat advances by `+2` (their partner); defender-takeover → dealer seat advances by `+1` (next clockwise seat, who is on the new dealer team).
payload.rationale: Standard Sheng Ji rotation. Keeps clockwise turn order while making teams alternate the dealer role within the team for retention, and handing the deal to the team that just took over for takeovers.
payload.alternatives_considered: always advance by +1 regardless of takeover; always advance by +2.
payload.why_not_alternatives: +1 means the same player keeps dealing on retention; +2 means after takeover the new dealer is on the wrong team.

payload.decision: Game over fires when the band-applied level advance would push the dealer team's level past A. We still emit the `roundSummary` showing the would-be advance, but set phase to `gameOver` instead of `scoring`. The winning team is the dealer team at the moment of advance.
payload.rationale: Brief says "If a team levels past A, show game over". This is the literal reading.
payload.alternatives_considered: cap the level at A (no game over); require landing exactly on A to win.
payload.why_not_alternatives: cap-no-game-over makes the game never end; require-exact-A complicates the bands.

payload.decision: Off-suit follow on a structured lead — when a follower has cards in the led effective suit but cannot match the structure: (a) for a pair lead, they must play all pairs of the led suit they hold first, then any singles of that suit, then off-suit fill to count; (b) for a tractor lead of length N pairs (2N cards), they must play all pairs of the led suit they hold up to N pairs, then any single cards of that suit up to remaining count, then off-suit fill. They are not required to play their *best* pairs/singles in the led suit, only sufficient cards from it.
payload.rationale: Standard Sheng Ji; the brief's wording maps to this. The "any pair / any single" relaxation avoids forcing greedy-play search.
payload.alternatives_considered: require the follower to play their highest cards in the led suit first.
payload.why_not_alternatives: not in the brief, harder to implement and to validate.

payload.decision: Server logs go to stdout (Node) at INFO level by default. No logging library; just a tiny `log.ts` wrapper around `console.log` with structured fields.
payload.rationale: No production deployment; stdout is enough.
payload.why_not_alternatives: adds dependency footprint with no payoff at this scale.

payload.decision: Vite proxies `/socket.io` and the REST surface (if any) to `http://localhost:3001` in dev. Production-mode Vite build is not configured (out of scope).
payload.rationale: Simplest cross-origin story for local dev.
payload.alternatives_considered: CORS-allow specific origins on the server.
payload.why_not_alternatives: CORS works too but the proxy is simpler and matches LAN play (one Vite-served URL).

payload.decision: Test-fixture loader is registered as a socket event (`__loadFixture`) gated by `process.env.NODE_ENV === "test"`. The check happens at handler registration so the event is *not registered at all* in dev / prod.
payload.rationale: Brief says "Do not expose fixture loading in normal development or production mode." Not registering the handler is stronger than rejecting calls at runtime.
payload.alternatives_considered: separate test-only HTTP endpoint; SQL injection of fixture state.
payload.why_not_alternatives: a registered-but-rejecting handler still announces the surface; SQL injection bypasses the socket layer the tests want to exercise.
